speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your bleeding, have you noticed bleeding from other sites, such as your gums when brushing or frequent nosebleeds? Additionally, is there a family history of bleeding disorders on either side of your family?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the family history of joint swelling and bleeding strongly suggests a factor deficiency like Hemophilia. To differentiate between Hemophilia A and B, I need to check your clotting times. REQUEST TEST: Partial_Thromboplastin_Time REQUEST TEST: Prothrombin_Time

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged PTT with a normal PT confirms a defect in the intrinsic pathway, which aligns with Hemophilia. To distinguish between Hemophilia A and B, I will check your specific factor levels. REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_LEVEL REQUEST TEST: Factor_IX_LEVEL

speaker: Doctor
text: Normal Factor VIII and IX levels effectively rule out Hemophilia A and B, which shifts our suspicion toward other causes like Von Willebrand Disease or platelet function disorders. Do you have a history of bleeding after minor cuts, and have you ever had your platelet count checked?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal factor levels, Von Willebrand Disease remains a strong possibility, especially with the family history. REQUEST TEST: Von_Willebrand_Factor_Antigen REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_Activity

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal vWF antigen and Factor VIII activity, Von Willebrand Disease is less likely, so I need to evaluate for platelet function disorders or rare coagulation defects. REQUEST TEST: Platelet_Count REQUEST TEST: Bleeding_Time

speaker: Doctor
text: The platelet count is normal, but the bleeding time of 6 minutes is prolonged, which points toward a primary hemostasis defect like a platelet function disorder rather than a coagulation factor deficiency. To differentiate between conditions like Glanzmann's thrombasthenia and Bernard-Soulier syndrome, I need to assess platelet aggregation. REQUEST TEST: Platelet_Aggregation_Study

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal platelet aggregation study is puzzling given the prolonged bleeding time and clinical symptoms of mucosal bleeding. I need to rule out acquired causes or specific functional defects not captured by standard aggregation, so I will check for inhibitors and von Willebrand factor ristocetin cofactor activity. REQUEST TEST: Ristocetin_Cofactor_Activity REQUEST TEST: Lupus_Anticoagulant

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal ristocetin cofactor activity and lupus anticoagulant, common causes like vWD and acquired inhibitors are ruled out, leaving a specific platelet function defect like Glanzmann's thrombasthenia as the most likely diagnosis given the clinical history. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann's thrombasthenia
